newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach revs pass "worst scenario" test.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach revs pass "worst scenario" test.

text.p: Stagecoach Plc, the transport group which delivered bumper profit growth in the last year, said on Friday it had measured itself against "worst case scenario" market conditions which reassured it that underlying earnings were of sufficient quality to survive.

Stagecoach measured the outlook of all its businesses against nightmare conditions of a market-slump, eight precent fall in passenger traffic and interest rates hitting 15 percent. Its efforts to reassure the market in turn come as some market players wonder whether the shares are over-valued at their current 799.5 pence level.
Brian Souter, executive chairman of Stagecoach, told Reuters that the conditions mirrored some of the worst seen in recent years.
In the case of Porterbrook, he said "a number of its customers would go bankrupt, but its business will be guaranteed by the government."

For the UK bus division, he said: "We have youngest fleet in Britain and we could afford to stop buying buses for two years, if necessary. We could reduce the size of our network to tailor it to supply and demand."

On the UK passenger rail franchise business, Stagecoach said of its South West Trains unit, "we made very conservative revenue assumptions at the outset, so even if the market fell by eight percent, we'd still be in profit."

For the overseas buses division, comprising mainly of Swebus, he said that some "revenue risk lies with the tendering authority and if rates rise we can then put this into new equations for future contracts."
"I'm not saying our business is risk or recession free - but these are great quality earnings if you put that tough test to them."
"Political and regulatory uncertainty are the only worries, but we're not as uncomfortable as we were 6 months ago."

However, longer-term issues of concern that remain include the fact that South West Trains' franchise term ends in 2003 and Porterbrook faces some of its current leasing deals ending around the same period.
